<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14f80e23957165f6fb23c2b3d59bdc7668652dfb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `853e69de48a50704c31b4ac616e3a2234ecc5761` — the merge of head `8304fb9e1307a9348065e2e761dcceaf9de55300` into base `14f80e23957165f6fb23c2b3d59bdc7668652dfb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 853e69de48a50704c31b4ac616e3a2234ecc5761 && git checkout 853e69de48a50704c31b4ac616e3a2234ecc5761
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 14f80e23957165f6fb23c2b3d59bdc7668652dfb 8304fb9e1307a9348065e2e761dcceaf9de55300 && git checkout -B drift-repro 14f80e23957165f6fb23c2b3d59bdc7668652dfb && git merge --no-ff 8304fb9e1307a9348065e2e761dcceaf9de55300

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14f80e23957165f6fb23c2b3d59bdc7668652dfb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 14f80e23957165f6fb23c2b3d59bdc7668652dfb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8304fb9e1307a9348065e2e761dcceaf9de55300`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read, via `gh api` (REST): card #20620 (body and all 4 comments: triage first grade `5888087153`, claim `5894939836`, os-dev-report `5895725152`, seat answer `5895765767`); PR #20691 (body, the 3-file list, the net diff against `main` at `14f80e2395`, and the head's whole `meta.ts` through the contents endpoint for the lines the diff does not show: the `--json` branch, the parse target, the exit paths); the check-runs on the head. Reference reads in the worktree, not of the PR: `AGENTS.md` §3 (Clause-②), `packages/cli/package.json` exports, `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/chain.ts`, `packages/spec/src/index.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts`, `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json`, `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md`, one earlier changeset for the Clause-② placement.

Check-runs on the head at read, 2026-09-29T18:06:45Z, newest run per name: 33 names. 28 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in), 2 in progress (Lint & Repo Gates; Test Core 3/6). 0 failed. Workflow runs on the head: 11 (8 success, 1 skipped, CI queued with shards still running, Lint & Type Check in progress). The two running checks are recorded as running; this record infers nothing for them, and the adopting seat reads them at adoption.

Binding direction: triage's first grade, direction 1 only (lead with the verdict and the refusals, then the applied mechanical edits, then the semantic notices, one header line counting each group; no notice dropped, ADR-0087 D3). Direction 2 is split to #20697 and direction 3 is out, per `5895765767`. The PR says `Part of #20620`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set: no change. The file list is `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts`, one new test beside it, one changeset. `packages/spec/**` is untouched, so no schema, conversion or semantic entry moved; the claim's read-only clause on spec held. RIGHT.

Public-surface changes the diff implies:
- (a) The human stdout of `os migrate meta --from N` (authored-source arm, text face): three groups reordered to verdict-and-refusals, applied, semantic; one content addition (the migrated stack's refusals under the verdict); the two schema-invalid verdict sentences reworded; the trailing blank line now follows the verdict at the top. RIGHT, judged in (1) to (4).
- (b) New module-level exports in `meta.ts`: `printMigrationReport`, `MigrationReport`, `MigrationRefusal`, and `PendingDataMigration` (was module-private). The package's exports map is `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, `./package.json`, and `src/index.ts` re-exports six migrate command classes but not `meta.js`, so none of these reaches a consumer: internal, no public API change. RIGHT.
- (c) `printPendingDataMigrations` now takes `readonly PendingDataMigration[]`: accepts a superset, internal. RIGHT.
- (d) `--json`, exit codes, `--out`, the loader's stderr: unchanged, judged in (3). RIGHT.
- (e) `meta.report-order.test.ts` in `src/commands/migrate/`, unit tier, beside the existing `meta.stored-flags.test.ts` precedent; `UNIT_FILES` is the tier walk's complement of the integration list. RIGHT.

(1) Byte-identity and order within group. The diff lifts the applied loop, the `--step` checkpoint loop, the semantic loop, the `--out` write and the data-migration advice out of `run()` into `printMigrationReport` with the three template strings character-identical on both sides of the hunk (the `    • path: from → to (conversionId)` line, the `    ⚠ [protocol N] surface → replacement` line with its `why:` and `verify:` lines, the `── protocol N ──` checkpoint), and each loop still iterates `result.applied`, `result.hops`, `result.todos` in chain order; no filter, sort, dedupe or rewording is introduced anywhere. Relative order inside the body is preserved: applied, then `--step` checkpoints, then semantic, then the `--out` line, then the advice. The only movement is the verdict block, from last to first, and on the empty-result path from after the advice to before the range answer. The SET pins in the new test derive the expected applied, notice and refusal lines from the chain's own data and compare with `toEqual`, and the last pin sorts every non-blank printed line against the union of headers, refusals, edits and notices, so a dropped, merged or reworded line has nowhere to hide behind a correct order. The dev's real-stack counts (applied 5=5, 0=0, 1=1; notice lines 744=744, 744=744, 996=996; `--step` and `--out` likewise) read consistently with the diff. So the change is order and headers only, plus the one addition in (2). RIGHT.

(2) The refusal group. The refusals are `parsed.error.issues` where `parsed = ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse(result.stack)` (head `meta.ts` line 580), the MIGRATED stack, the same parse that feeds `schemaValid` in `--json`. The loader's `[authored-source] defineStack()` list (in `config.ts`, untouched, on stderr) is of the stack as authored and still names the keys the chain converts: on the dev's h1 stack it has 6 issues, the report's group the 2 left after the chain. Since every listed edit is a D2 conversion that `defineStack` already applies at load (triage), what blocks the stack is the post-chain set, so the migrated stack's issues are the right set, and the header says "left after the chain" so the two lists cannot be read as one. Within direction 1: the direction reads "lead with the verdict and the refusals", the printer had no refusal list to lead with (the card's "41 refusals" were the loader's stderr interleaved on the terminal), so listing them is the smallest change that executes the direction as written; the seat's answer `5895765767` already named it as the one content addition for this review to judge. The renderer is `formatZodIssue`, exported from `@objectstack/spec`'s index and the loader's own renderer, so a refusal reads the same in both places. RIGHT.

Header count. The invalid verdict carries the count (`N refusals left after the chain`); the valid verdict `Migrated stack is schema-valid` carries no number, which is the zero. The applied and semantic headers print only when their group is non-empty, exactly as before. One header line per populated group holds. RIGHT, with that note.

(3) `--json`, exit codes, `--out`, loader stderr. `--json`: the `if (flags.json) { await emitJson({...}); if (flags.out) writeFileSync(...); return; }` block (head lines 584 to 617) is outside every diff hunk and returns before the human branch; its keys, values and array order come from the same `result`, so unchanged. Exit codes: neither the old nor the new human branch calls `this.exit`; the catch block is outside the hunks; a schema-invalid run still exits 0 (as `test/migrate-meta-default-range.test.ts` records). `--out`: written at the same place (after the semantic group, before the advice) with the same `resolve(flags.out)`, and, as before, not written on the empty-result path (pre-existing, not touched). Loader stderr: `packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts` is not in the file list. RIGHT.

(4) The two reworded sentences. Old A ended "resolve the manual changes above, then run `os validate`."; new A reads "N refusals left after the chain. Resolve them, then run `os validate`:" and the refusal lines follow. "Them" names the lines printed directly under it, which are exactly the migrated stack's parse issues, so it is true in the new order, and more accurate than the old, which pointed at advisories rather than at what fails the parse. Old B (no hop) ended "Widen the range above, or run `os validate` for the refusals."; new B reads "nothing here has been fixed; N refusals, exactly as the source has them:", the refusals follow, then the range answer. With zero hops `applyMetaMigrations` returns `stack: current` with `current` never reassigned (`chain.ts`), so the migrated stack IS the normalized source and "exactly as the source has them" is true; the "widen the range above" pointer is dropped rather than inverted, and the range answer follows it (pinned: the range-answer index is greater than the verdict index). The valid verdict is unchanged. RIGHT.

(5) Ablation. The test file is 3 ORDER pins, 1 header-count pin, 4 SET pins, 8 in all. With the verdict moved back to last, ORDER 1 fails at `expect(verdict).toBe(0)` (the quoted "expected 1030 to be +0"), ORDER 2 at `lines[0]`, ORDER 3 at the same index pin; the header-count pin filters by regex and the SET pins compare arrays derived from the chain data or slice from the semantic header, none reading a cross-group position, so all 5 stay green. 3 red and 5 green is what the mutation must produce, and the dev's reading matches. The ablated blob `1a002a9b` is the head blob of `meta.ts` (the diff's index line reads `e80aee74e3..1a002a9b48`), so the ablation was of the file under review. It proves what it claims: the order pins bite on the reorder and the set pins do not. That the set pins bite on a dropped notice is by construction (`toEqual` against chain-derived arrays), not by ablation, and the PR claims no more. RIGHT. The changeset is judged in ②.

(6) `Part of #20620`. The card keeps direction 2 (the printer's pairing) pending on #20697 and the seat said the card stays open for it; a closing keyword would auto-close the card at merge, strand direction 2 and leave the pm labels behind. `Part of` with no closing keyword is right; the check-runs "Part-of PR must not also close its card" and "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" are green. RIGHT.

Wrong: none found.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20620-migrate-meta-verdict-first.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': patch`, body carries `Clause-②: no`, matching the PR body. What the diff publishes: a behaviour change to the human text face of one command (order, one added group, two reworded lines); the machine face (`--json`), the exit codes, the `--out` snapshot and stderr unchanged; no authorable key added or removed, no export reachable through the package's exports map, nothing removed or renamed. A fix in a released package takes `patch`, never `skip-changeset` (AGENTS.md §3), and a reordered human report publishes nothing more than that. Check Changeset: success. RIGHT.

Clause-②: no — right. Nothing an author can write is added or removed, so `no`; and no arm, since `no (widening)` is malformed.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions[0]`, the shape of direction 2's structured link (A/B/C/D): ANSWERED by the seat in `5895765767`. Filed bare as #20697 with the dev's option A carried as the proposal; the shape is the spec seat's. Nothing for this PR.

Deviations (5), all declared, all ANSWERED:
1. The draft PR was created with `gh pr create` (GraphQL, not REST): process only, no contract effect.
2. The first label-write ran outside with-fleet, exit 3, nothing written; the re-run wrote once, read back.
3. app-showcase would not load in the worktree; measured on app-crm plus two scratch stacks (h1: refusals, applied edits and notices; dm: the data-migration advice under `--from 16`). The three together exercise every group and the advice's placement.
4. Integration and nightly runs cited at `7c484d891f`: `packages/cli` is identical at `8304fb9e13` (the diff's head blob `1a002a9b48` is the blob ablated there).
5. A detached base worktree for the before-readings, removed at cleanup.

Declared narrowing, verification run unlocked (no `flock` on macOS): declared, not silent; the check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts in any case. ANSWERED.

PR-context gates NOT MEASURED locally (single-claim paths, part-of closing keyword, closing-target claim): ANSWERED by the head's check-runs, all success: "No other open PR may claim the same issue", "No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path", "Part-of PR must not also close its card", "The card this PR closes must claim this branch".

`out_of_scope_findings`:
- class a, `os migrate meta` aborts at load on an `ObjectSchema.create` object carrying a retired key: filed by the seat as #20696. ANSWERED.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json`, item `cli.migrate-meta-codemod` (revision 3), step 7 quotes the old warning verbatim ("resolve the manual changes above, then run `os validate`"): confirmed stale after this PR; the item's acceptance clause (the verdict agrees with `schemaValid`) still holds and the checklist watchdog is green. ESCALATED to the seat: outside the claim's file surface, it needs a revision-4 bump and a history entry by the checklist's author (the `checklist-author` skill is the tool), and the step should name the refusal group so a runner knows the list now exists.
- `skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md` lines 139 to 147 list Applied, manual, schema-valid and data migrations under "What it prints:": no order is claimed and every quoted string still prints (confirmed); a governed surface (Tier H), untouched, Governed Surface Queue Guard green. ESCALATED as a one-line reorder for that surface's next queue entry; not blocking.
- `check:platform-checklist` red on `main` (identity-auth `twoFactor`): pre-existing, maintainer-run, out of per-PR CI, not this PR. ANSWERED.
- Two published-subpath pins red on macOS only (`/var` versus `/private/var`), reproduced on a clean base worktree: host-only; CI is Linux and the Test Core shards answer for it (one still running at read). ANSWERED.

Semantic notice, mine: with stderr and stdout on one terminal an upgrader now sees two refusal lists, the loader's as-authored list before the chain and the report's post-chain list, with different counts. The report's "left after the chain" and the loader's `[authored-source]` prefix keep them apart; noted for the seat, nothing asked of this PR.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20620-migrate-meta-order`
Reviewed-by: `local_1d2a197c-c20e-4e90-9be8-413d4d432289`

**VERDICT: PASS**
